provenance_families.label: selective prediction, risk control, and calibration
provenance_families.independence_basis: Distinct external statistical-learning authors and institutions; all artifacts predate this AQ9 lineage and were produced without this repository.

provenance_families.label: staged conditional computation and early exit
provenance_families.independence_basis: Two independent primary method papers from distinct author teams and eras on hierarchical mixture gating and neural early exit; both predate AQ9 and are external to this repository.

provenance_families.label: local multi-label classification and modular decomposition
provenance_families.independence_basis: Independent work from Waikato and Allen Institute collaborators on multi-label transformation and modular language-model reasoning.

provenance_families.label: adversarial prompt and control-data isolation
provenance_families.independence_basis: Separate security research teams from Berkeley, OpenAI, Google, Google DeepMind, and ETH Zurich with distinct defenses and threat models.

sources.title: Selective Classification for Deep Neural Networks
sources.provenance_owner: Yonatan Geifman and Ran El-Yaniv; arXiv
supported_claims: Selective classification separates a predictor from an acceptance function and evaluates conditional error against accepted coverage.
Under the paper's independent and identically distributed labeled-sample assumptions, confidence-ranked acceptance supports a high-probability selective-risk bound.
unsupported_extrapolations: No per-case correctness, distribution-shift robustness, adversarial robustness, language-model routing, or H5 efficacy follows from this source.
uncertainties: Coverage depends on ranking quality, and the paper's supervised image-classification setting does not establish transfer to unresolved-decision selection.

sources.title: Conformal Risk Control
sources.provenance_owner: Anastasios N. Angelopoulos, Stephen Bates, Adam Fisch, Lihua Lei, and Tal Schuster; arXiv
supported_claims: The paper gives finite-sample expected control for bounded monotone losses under its exchangeability and regularity conditions.
unsupported_extrapolations: Expected risk control is not per-instance correctness and does not automatically define or validate an H5 loss or mechanism.
uncertainties: Any later application would have to establish exchangeability, boundedness, monotonicity, and the exact loss before invoking the result.

sources.title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
sources.provenance_owner: Chuan Guo, Geoff Pleiss, Yu Sun, and Kilian Q. Weinberger; PMLR

identity.proceedings_identity: Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 70:1321-1330, ICML 2017

supported_claims: The studied modern neural networks were empirically miscalibrated, and temperature scaling was effective on most tested image and document datasets.
unsupported_extrapolations: Temperature scaling alone does not establish selective-risk control, shifted-distribution robustness, or H5 correctness.
uncertainties: Calibration quality is dataset and model dependent, and the source does not study anonymous unresolved-decision selection.

sources.title: Can You Trust Your Model's Uncertainty? Evaluating Predictive Uncertainty Under Dataset Shift
sources.provenance_owner: Yaniv Ovadia and coauthors; arXiv and NeurIPS 2019

identity.proceedings_identity: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 2019

supported_claims: Across the paper's benchmark, accuracy and calibration degraded under dataset shift, and ordinary post-hoc calibration could fall short.
unsupported_extrapolations: The empirical benchmark does not provide a universal uncertainty guarantee or validate any H5 route selector.
uncertainties: The benchmark covers supervised classification shifts, not the future distribution or structure of an H5 evaluation.

sources.title: Hierarchical Mixtures of Experts and the EM Algorithm
sources.provenance_owner: Michael I. Jordan and Robert A. Jacobs; Neural Computation and the Berkeley author archive

artifact.version: Wayback timestamp 20230521045924 immutable capture of the author-hosted primary PostScript

supported_claims: The paper presents a tree-structured supervised hierarchical mixture in which gating coefficients and expert components are learned, including expectation-maximization and online learning procedures.
unsupported_extrapolations: Robot-dynamics simulations with generalized linear models do not establish sparse hard language-model routing, H5 performance, or safety.
uncertainties: Soft mixture behavior, supervised training assumptions, and the historical task domain may not transfer to unresolved-decision selection.

sources.title: BranchyNet: Fast Inference via Early Exiting from Deep Neural Networks
sources.provenance_owner: Surat Teerapittayanon, Bradley McDanel, and H. T. Kung; arXiv
supported_claims: Side classifiers permit confidence-gated early exits for easier tested samples while later layers process harder samples, creating an empirical accuracy-latency tradeoff.
unsupported_extrapolations: Vision early-exit results do not establish an H5 routing benefit, calibrated gates, or language-model safety.
uncertainties: An early stage can be confidently wrong, so stage-conditional error and propagation require prospective measurement.

sources.title: Classifier Chains for Multi-label Classification
sources.provenance_owner: Jesse Read, Bernhard Pfahringer, Geoffrey Holmes, and Eibe Frank; University of Waikato Research Commons

artifact.version: ECML PKDD 2009 author-accepted manuscript deposited under DOI 10.1007/978-3-642-04174-7_17

supported_claims: An ordered chain of binary label classifiers can model label correlations with competitive empirical predictive and time complexity on the studied multi-label datasets.
unsupported_extrapolations: The source does not establish H5 performance, security, abstention, or immunity to chain-order error propagation.
uncertainties: Order sensitivity and dependence on earlier predictions are prospective risks rather than assumed benefits.

sources.title: Decomposed Prompting: A Modular Approach for Solving Complex Tasks
sources.provenance_owner: Tushar Khot and coauthors; arXiv and ICLR 2023
supported_claims: A decomposer can delegate simpler subtasks to independently replaceable or recursively decomposed prompt, model, or symbolic modules, with gains on the studied GPT-3 reasoning tasks.
unsupported_extrapolations: The studied reasoning gains do not prove route-selection, abstention, calibration, security, or H5 improvement.
uncertainties: Decomposer and recomposition errors can dominate, and the evaluated tasks do not match anonymous unresolved-decision selection.

sources.title: StruQ: Defending Against Prompt Injection with Structured Queries
sources.provenance_owner: Sizhe Chen, Julien Piet, Chawin Sitawarin, and David Wagner; USENIX Association
supported_claims: The paper separates prompt and data channels with a filtering front end and structured instruction tuning, improving resistance on its tested attacks with little or no measured utility loss.
unsupported_extrapolations: The source does not provide worst-case security or blanket coverage of multi-turn, jailbreak, tool-effect, or unseen adaptive attacks.
uncertainties: The final paper reports nonzero success for optimization-based attacks and explicitly does not establish full security.

sources.title: The Instruction Hierarchy: Training LLMs to Prioritize Privileged Instructions
sources.provenance_owner: Eric Wallace, Kai Xiao, Reimar Leike, Lilian Weng, Johannes Heidecke, and Alex Beutel; arXiv
supported_claims: Training GPT-3.5 to prioritize system over user and third-party instructions improved measured robustness, including on some attack types held out from training.
unsupported_extrapolations: The model-level defense is not a formal or general prompt-injection security guarantee and does not validate H5.
uncertainties: Robustness and over-refusal remain dependent on the model, generated training data, and evaluated attack distribution.

sources.title: Defeating Prompt Injections by Design
supported_claims: CaMeL separates trusted-query control-flow generation from quarantined untrusted-data handling and enforces capability and data-flow policies at tool calls within its threat model.
The paper reports 77 percent AgentDojo task completion with its stated security property, compared with 84 percent completion for the undefended system.
unsupported_extrapolations: The result does not cover compromised trusted prompts or memory, every text-only manipulation, phishing, or security outside explicit policies and the stated threat model.
uncertainties: Utility, policy completeness, trusted-query assumptions, and clarification requirements remain material deployment constraints.

cross_source_tensions.statement: Post-hoc calibration can be effective on studied in-distribution datasets while still falling short under dataset shift.
Selective or conformal risk statements depend on sampling, exchangeability, loss, and ranking assumptions that shifted data can violate.
Hierarchical or confidence-gated routing can specialize or save computation, but learned gates and miscalibrated confidence can still route incorrectly.
Local or modular decomposition can expose structure while ordering, decomposer, and recomposition errors can propagate globally.
Measured prompt-injection robustness remains bounded by model, training data, policy, benchmark, and threat-model assumptions; none establishes universal immunity.

mechanism_families.label: empirically calibrated selective prediction and risk control
mechanism_families.non_isomorphism_to_h4: Acceptance is constrained by externally measured risk, coverage, calibration, or set loss rather than H4 graph topology and categorical graph uncertainty.
supported_constraints: Any use of confidence requires an explicit calibration and shift evaluation.
Any claimed risk control must state and verify its sampling, loss, and monotonicity assumptions.
unsupported_extrapolations: The evidence does not choose a score, acceptance rule, loss, calibration sample, or operating point.

mechanism_families.label: staged conditional routing and early exit
mechanism_families.non_isomorphism_to_h4: Sequential gates create path-dependent conditional computation; H4 uses one whole-case joint extraction followed by deterministic graph-root resolution.
supported_constraints: Stage-conditional errors, exit behavior, and compute cost must be observed separately.
Early confidence must not be assumed correct without calibration evidence.
unsupported_extrapolations: The evidence does not choose a stage count, gate, exit rule, model call, or routing hierarchy.

mechanism_families.label: local classification or modular decomposition and recomposition
mechanism_families.non_isomorphism_to_h4: Multiple localized label or subtask decisions are composed, rather than jointly extracting every candidate state and pairwise relation before graph resolution.
supported_constraints: Local accuracy, decomposition validity, recomposition consistency, ordering, and propagation require separate observation.
Modularity is supported only if failures remain attributable and bounded.
unsupported_extrapolations: The evidence does not choose subtasks, order, module interfaces, recomposition, prompts, or model allocation.

mechanism_families.label: privilege-separated prompt, control, and data architecture
mechanism_families.non_isomorphism_to_h4: The family changes trust boundaries and information or control flow through separate channels, privilege levels, quarantine, or enforcement rather than changing H4's output graph.
supported_constraints: Untrusted instructions require an explicit provenance and privilege boundary.
Security claims must bind a threat model, policies, adaptive attacks, benign utility, and unauthorized effects.
unsupported_extrapolations: The evidence does not choose channel syntax, privilege levels, models, policies, interpreter behavior, or a security claim for H5.

prospective_discriminators.observable: Accepted-case error and accepted coverage across preregistered acceptance settings.
prospective_discriminators.falsifying_observation: Tighter acceptance fails to trade coverage for lower accepted error on held-out data.
prospective_discriminators.claim_boundary: A curve is diagnostic evidence only and does not establish population or per-case correctness.

prospective_discriminators.observable: Reliability and accepted-case error on held-out in-distribution and prespecified shift slices.
prospective_discriminators.falsifying_observation: Apparent calibration or selective performance collapses on the held-out shift slices.
prospective_discriminators.claim_boundary: Observed robustness remains limited to the frozen slices and exact evaluation conditions.

prospective_discriminators.observable: Exit-depth distribution, stage-conditional error, calls, latency, and early false-exit propagation.
prospective_discriminators.falsifying_observation: Cases do not separate by stage difficulty or early exits create disproportionate false decisions.
prospective_discriminators.claim_boundary: The observation cannot by itself justify a stage design or deployment latency claim.

prospective_discriminators.observable: Per-local decision error, exact-set and per-label error, decomposition validity, recomposition consistency, ordering sensitivity, and propagation.
prospective_discriminators.falsifying_observation: A localized failure routinely contaminates unrelated outputs or recomposition dominates the error budget.
prospective_discriminators.claim_boundary: Locality evidence does not choose a decomposition or prove global efficacy.

prospective_discriminators.observable: Adaptive injection success, benign utility, privileged-instruction retention, false blocks, and clarification rate under a frozen threat model.
prospective_discriminators.falsifying_observation: Untrusted payload instructions redirect privileged behavior or the defense destroys benign utility.
prospective_discriminators.claim_boundary: Results remain bounded to the exact attacks, models, policies, and threat model.

prospective_discriminators.observable: Control-flow invariance and unauthorized tool or data-flow effects when untrusted payload instructions vary.
prospective_discriminators.falsifying_observation: Untrusted instructions alter privileged control flow outside explicitly authorized data dependencies.
prospective_discriminators.claim_boundary: Passing a policy-bound check is not universal prompt-injection security.
